0: Sound of wind through the canopy.
The path I marked is already closing.
Something moved through the understory. Held still.
Following a deer path. Goes exactly where I needed.
Rain started. The canopy is holding most of it.
The fern layer is thick. Good soil under it.
Something ahead went quiet. Waited. Kept moving.
1: Past the line where the loggers usually stop. Trees larger here.
Found a stand untouched by axes for a long time. The trees are taller for it.
Roots in the path the size of my shoulder. Stepped carefully.
An old blaze on a trunk, weathered grey. Whoever marked it did not come back.
Deeper now. The light reaches the ground in pieces.
Trees here grow on top of other trees. Some are still alive under the new ones.
Smelled smoke a long way off. Did not investigate. The trees would not have liked it.
Found a clearing with three trees standing in the middle. The clearing made the trees mean something.
Walked through a stand where every trunk was a different age. A whole century, side by side.
Older wood, harder work. Worth it, mostly.
2: The old-growth. Cathedral wood. Worked quietly.
Trees here older than the wolves who have ever seen them.
Found a trunk wider than my whole length. Took only the lower branches.
Moss on the north sides three fingers deep. Knew the way home without looking.
Walked among trees that had never been counted.
A stand the loggers do not know about. The stand prefers it this way.
Light came through the canopy in beams, like the sun was choosing where to land.
The deepest wood. The work, here, requires a kind of respect.
Found a tree split by lightning a hundred years ago, still living. Did not take any of it.
The far trees. The ones that remember when there were more of them.

light: Roots tangled the path. Lost time.
Rain made the bark slick. Careful work.
The path I marked was already grown over.
Ant nest at the base of the tree. Worked around it. Mostly.
Sap dripped on the paw and stayed. The paw was sticky for hours.
Wasp investigating the fresh cut. Stepped back. Politely.
Wind picked up. The next tree did not want to fall the way I wanted.
Mosquitoes thick as smoke. Worked through them. Itched for days.
moderate: Tree fell the wrong way. Close call.
A root caught my back foot. Went down hard.
Something in the dark forest did not want me there.
Disturbed a nest I did not see. Moved before counting.
Falling branch I had not noticed. Noticed it. Late.
The tree leaned wrong all morning. It fell wrong, accordingly.
Stepped on a wasp ground-nest. Ran. The ground-nest is still angry.
Trunk twisted as it fell, caught a paw under it. Worked free.
Sap in the eye. Worked one-eyed for a while.
severe: Bear investigating my woodpile. Then investigating me.
The dry grass caught from a spark. Not so controlled.
Tree came down on top of me. Working out from under it.
The mud swallowed me to the hip. Took time to extract.
Something large, very close, very fast. Dropped everything and ran.
Tree split as it fell. The split end went where I had been standing. Where I no longer was.
Fell from a low branch the wrong way. The wrong way was longer than expected.
Wildfire on the next ridge over. Worked downhill, fast.
Something in the deep wood took an interest. Worked elsewhere.
Trunk rolled down the slope after I cut it. Rolled further than the slope had any right to.

no_tool: No edge left to swing. Coming back.
Nothing to fell with. Going home.
precious_break: Axe too precious to break. Heading back.
Cannot let the enchanted axe end this way. Coming back with it.
The good axe stays. Heading home before it goes.
Will not spend the last of this one. Bringing it back.
Too well-made to lose to a tree. Going home with it intact.
broken: Head came clean off. Bag lighter by one tool.
Haft split down the grain. Done.
Last swing went into the haft instead of the wood. Gone.
The axe was finished before the tree was. The axe wins, in a way.
last_gone: Bag holds no more wood-work. Going home.
End of the cutting. Coming back.
Nothing left to fell with. Turning toward the bed.
switched_spare: Set down the worn axe. Picked up the next.
Spare axe in the bag. Using it now.
Old axe aside. New axe in paw.
Picked up the second axe. Carried on.
nearly_done: Axe-iron worn thin. Going home before it gives.
Last few cuts left in this one. Saving them.
Axe is tired. So am I. Walking home.
Almost spent. Coming back before it finishes.
